category_title: Students with ASD and learning difficulties who prioritize neatness over speed
scenario_title: Mental math game on Nintendo DS with stylus
minimal_context: The student is using a stylus to answer math sums in the x20 game on a Nintendo DS.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: It is time to do the x20 math game on your Nintendo DS. Please begin answering the sums.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Sits looking at the Nintendo DS screen without starting the activity, waiting to be told what to do.)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Go ahead and start writing your answers.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Slowly and carefully writes the first answer with the stylus, taking a long time to ensure the numbers are perfectly neat.)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Okay, try the next math sum.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Writes an incorrect answer, looks away from the screen, and then immediately restarts the entire x20 game from the beginning.)

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: It is time to do the x20 math game on your Nintendo DS. Please begin answering the sums.

STUDENT: (Sits looking at the Nintendo DS screen without starting the activity, waiting to be told what to do.)

TUTOR: Go ahead and start writing your answers.

STUDENT: (Slowly and carefully writes the first answer with the stylus, taking a long time to ensure the numbers are perfectly neat.)

TUTOR: Okay, try the next math sum.

STUDENT: (Writes an incorrect answer, looks away from the screen, and then immediately restarts the entire x20 game from the beginning.)

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: if she answered an item incorrectly
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: would tend to restart the x20

behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: verbal prompting was required to initiate her use of the DSs and to help her understand the tasks
very preoccupied with writing neatly and correctly and this slowed her response rate
